entities.summary:
Mario Lago was an Italian statesman and diplomat who played a significant role in the development of modern Italy. Born into a lower-middle-class family, Lago rose through the ranks of the Italian government to become a key figure in the country's early post-war reconstruction efforts.

As Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1948 to 1950, Lago was instrumental in shaping Italy's foreign policy and negotiating key trade agreements with European powers. His diplomatic efforts helped establish Italy as a major player on the world stage, paving the way for its rapid economic growth and industrialization in the decades that followed.

Despite his significant contributions to Italian politics, Lago's life was cut short when he died on April 27, 1950, at the age of 55. His legacy continues to be felt in Italy today, with many regarding him as a pioneering figure in the country's modern diplomatic history.
